title: High Molecular Weight DNA Extraction for Long-Read Sequencing
author: Kanae Nishii
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bempjc5n
materials: Leave at 50 °C for 1 hour. 50 °C High molecular weight DNA should be dissolved very gently to avoid shearing. We incubate the samples at 50 °C in a ThermoMixer with gentle agitation at 300 rpm.
Pre-cool the pestle and mortar with liquid nitrogen.
Carefully discard supernatant without dislodging the pellet.
Leave the tubes at 50 °C, 300 rpm in a ThermoMixer for 1 hour. 50 °C

steps.title: Prepare buffers and equipment on ice
steps.instruction: Prepare 200 ml Nuclei Isolation Buffer (NIB) and keep on ice; prepare 20 ml NIB base‑Triton mix and keep on ice; prepare 60 ml Sorbitol buffer; prepare six 50 ml Falcon tubes layered with 40 µm gauge cell strainers and keep on ice.

steps.title: Set up liquid nitrogen and mortar
steps.instruction: Fill a suitable dewar with liquid nitrogen; place mortar and pestle in a fume hood and keep pre‑cooled.

steps.title: Grind leaf tissue in liquid nitrogen
steps.instruction: Cut 1–2 g fresh leaf tissue, place in liquid nitrogen to shock‑freeze, transfer to the pre‑cooled mortar, add liquid nitrogen to cover the tissue and grind until a fine powder forms; once the liquid nitrogen evaporates, grind more vigorously for 30 s; repeat the addition of liquid nitrogen and grinding two more times (total three grinding cycles).

steps.title: Resuspend ground tissue in NIB and Triton
steps.instruction: Transfer the frozen powder to a beaker of cold NIB on ice using a pre‑cooled spatula, swirl gently; add 1/20 volume of the NIB base‑Triton mix, close the tubes with lids and mix by gentle swirling and inverting.

steps.title: Pellet nuclei by low‑speed centrifugation
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the suspension at 2 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C (if possible).

steps.title: Wash pellet with Sorbitol buffer
steps.instruction: Add 10 ml Sorbitol buffer to each pellet, swirl to mix, then centrifuge at 3 000 × g for 10 min at 4 °C (if possible).

steps.title: Discard supernatant and keep nuclei pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant carefully, leaving the pellet undisturbed; invert tubes on tissue to remove traces of buffer without losing the pellet. The pellet may be stored at –80 °C (not recommended).

steps.title: Lyse nuclei with Buffer G2 and additives
steps.instruction: Add 5 ml QIAGEN Buffer G2 to each 50 ml Falcon tube containing the nuclei pellet and gently resuspend; add 0.1 % β‑mercaptoethanol (5 µl) and a pinch of PVPP, then swirl to mix.

steps.title: Pre‑heat water bath to 50 °C
steps.instruction: Set a water bath to 50 °C and keep it ready for subsequent steps.

steps.title: Incubate lysate at 50 °C for 5 min
steps.instruction: Incubate the tube(s) at 50 °C for 5 minutes.

steps.title: Add RNase and Proteinase K
steps.instruction: Add 10 µl RNase A (or 50 µl RNase A/T1 Mix) and 100 µl QIAGEN Proteinase K to each tube, swirling gently after each addition.

steps.title: Incubate digestion at 50 °C >5 h
steps.instruction: Incubate the lysate at 50 °C for more than 5 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Prepare filtration setup on ice
steps.instruction: Place the six 50 ml Falcon tubes (prepared earlier) on ice; ensure each tube has a 40 µm gauge cell strainer on top.

steps.title: Filter lysate through 100 µm mesh
steps.instruction: Filter the NIB/sample suspension through a 100 µm nylon mesh filter by gravity; do not force the sample through; replace the filter when clogged. Keep the filtrate on ice.

steps.title: Filter filtrate through 40 µm mesh
steps.instruction: Filter the 100 µm filtrate through a 40 µm nylon mesh filter by gravity; replace the filter when clogged. Keep the filtrate on ice.

steps.title: Aliquot filtrate into six Falcon tubes
steps.instruction: Divide the final filtrate equally into the six Falcon tubes, adding 40–50 ml to each tube. Keep on ice.

steps.title: Label Genomic‑tip tubes and pre‑heat Buffer QF
steps.instruction: Label five 50 ml Falcon tubes (without lids) as: 1 = QBT, 2 = Sample, 3 = QC 1, 4 = QC 2, 5 = Final Sample (use a new tube for Final Sample). Pre‑heat Buffer QF to 50 °C in the water bath.

steps.title: Equilibrate Genomic‑tip with Buffer QBT
steps.instruction: Place a QIAGEN Genomic‑tip 100/G column in its holder on top of tube 1 (QBT) and add 4 ml Buffer QBT; allow the column to empty by gravity flow without forcing the remaining buffer through.

steps.title: Load lysate onto Genomic‑tip column
steps.instruction: Move the column to tube 2 (Sample) and apply up to 5 ml of the clear lysate (supernatant) to the equilibrated column; allow gravity flow. Do not load more than 7 ml total lysate per column.

steps.title: Wash column with Buffer QC
steps.instruction: Move the column to tube 3 (QC 1) and add 7.5 ml Buffer QC; allow gravity flow. Then move to tube 4 (QC 2) and add another 7.5 ml Buffer QC; allow gravity flow. Traces of Buffer QC will not affect elution.

steps.title: Elute DNA with pre‑warmed Buffer QF
steps.instruction: Move the column to tube 5 (Final Sample) and add 5 ml Buffer QF pre‑warmed to 50 °C; allow the buffer to flow through by gravity. Store the eluted DNA on ice; the column can be reused twice for the same sample (stable up to six hours from first equilibration).

steps.title: Transfer eluate to 2 ml tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer the DNA eluate to 2 ml Eppendorf tubes, adding 1 ml per tube (total of 30 tubes from the 30 ml elution, i.e., 5 ml Buffer QF × 6 tubes).

steps.title: Centrifuge eluate at 11 000 rpm
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the 2 ml tubes at 11 000 rpm for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Precipitate DNA with isopropanol
steps.instruction: Add 700 µl ice‑cold isopropanol to each tube and gently invert to mix.

steps.title: Incubate precipitation at –20 °C >2 h
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes at –20 °C for more than 2 hours or overnight.

steps.title: Wash pellet with 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Discard the supernatant (retain until pellet recovery is verified), add 400 µl ice‑cold 70 % ethanol to each tube, then centrifuge at 11 000 rpm for 10 minutes.

steps.title: Remove ethanol and air‑dry pellet
steps.instruction: Discard the ethanol supernatant by tipping the tube with the pellet on the upper side over a clean beaker; invert tubes on tissue to remove residual ethanol; air‑dry the pellet for 10–20 minutes (do not overdry).

steps.title: Resuspend pellet in TE buffer
steps.instruction: Add 50 µl TE buffer (or any desired downstream buffer) to each tube; if the pellet is not visible, apply the buffer to the side where the pellet is expected, gently flick the tube to rinse; do not pipet or vortex the DNA.

steps.title: Pool DNA into two tubes
steps.instruction: Collect the DNA from the 30 tubes (50 µl each, total 1.5 ml) into two 2 ml tubes, adding 750 µl to each tube; optionally check concentration with a NanoDrop.

steps.title: Add NaOAc and isopropanol for second precipitation
steps.instruction: To each tube add 1/10 volume (75 µl) of 3 M NaOAc and an equal volume (825 µl) of ice‑cold isopropanol.

steps.title: Incubate second precipitation at –20 °C >1 h
steps.instruction: Leave the tubes at –20 °C for more than 1 hour or overnight.

steps.title: Centrifuge and discard supernatant
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 11 000 rpm for 10 minutes, discard the supernatant, and invert tubes on tissue to remove residual ethanol.

steps.title: Air‑dry pellet and final elution
steps.instruction: Air‑dry the pellet for 10–20 minutes (do not overdry) and elute in an appropriate volume of elution buffer (e.g., 50 µl TE) to obtain a concentration >100 ng/µl for PacBio sequencing.

steps.title: Perform DNA quality and quantity assessments
steps.instruction: Assess DNA integrity by 0.8 % agarose gel electrophoresis or Agilent TapeStation; assess quality by spectrophotometric OD values (NanoDrop or DeNovix); assess quantity by fluorometry (Qubit or DeNovix). Optionally measure residual RNA with Qubit RNA HS assay.

steps.title: Repeat grinding and extraction for remaining tissue
steps.instruction: Repeat steps 3–12 (grinding, NIB/Triton addition, centrifugations, Buffer G2 lysis, incubations) until all leaf material is processed; the suspension should be smooth with no clumps.
